title: Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons, like rain clouds, appear in the world. What four? And how, bhikkhus, is a person with thunder but no…
content: Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons, like rain clouds, appear in the world. What four? And how, bhikkhus, is a person with thunder but no rain? Here, bhikkhus, a person speaks but does not act. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with thunder but no rain. And how, bhikkhus, is a person with rain but no thunder? Here, bhikkhus, a person acts but does not speak. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with rain but no thunder. And how, bhikkhus, is a person with neither thunder nor rain? Here, bhikkhus, a person neither speaks nor acts. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with neither thunder nor rain. And how, bhikkhus, is a person with both thunder and rain? Here, bhikkhus, a person speaks and acts. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with both thunder and rain. Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons, like rain clouds, appear in the world.

title: Sona, when energy is overstrained, it leads to restlessness; when energy is too lax, it leads to laziness. Therefore, Sona, you should establish energy in…
content: Sona, when energy is overstrained, it leads to restlessness; when energy is too lax, it leads to laziness. Therefore, Sona, you should establish energy in balance, penetrate the faculties in balance, and there grasp the sign.

title: But this abiding, Ānanda, has been fully realized by the Tathāgata, that is, by not attending to any sign, he attains and abides in internal…
content: But this abiding, Ānanda, has been fully realized by the Tathāgata, that is, by not attending to any sign, he attains and abides in internal voidness. And if, Ānanda, while the Tathāgata is abiding in this abiding, bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, laymen, laywomen, kings, ministers, wanderers, disciples of wanderers come to see him, then, Ānanda, the Tathāgata, with mind inclined towards seclusion, tending towards seclusion, gravitating towards seclusion, living alone, delighting in renunciation, making an end of all states that are based on the taints, speaks only words that are encouraging.

title: - What is good that does not age? What is good that is eternal? What is the treasure of humans? What cannot be taken by…
content:
- What is good that does not age?
What is good that is eternal?
What is the treasure of humans?
What cannot be taken by thieves?
- Virtue is good that does not age,
Faith is good that is eternal,
Wisdom is the treasure of humans,
Merit cannot be taken by thieves.

title: Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possessing three things has overcome Māra's power and shines like the sun. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possesses the Arahant's aggregate…
content:
Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possessing three things has overcome Māra's power and shines like the sun. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possesses the Arahant's aggregate of virtue, the Arahant's aggregate of concentration, and the Arahant's aggregate of wisdom. Possessing these three things, a bhikkhu has overcome Māra's power and shines like the sun.

Virtue, concentration, and wisdom —
For one who has well developed these,
Having overcome Māra's power,
He shines and blazes like the sun.

title: And what, bhikkhus, is the noble seeking? Here, bhikkhus, a person, being subject to birth himself, having understood the danger in what is subject to…
content: And what, bhikkhus, is the noble seeking? Here, bhikkhus, a person, being subject to birth himself, having understood the danger in what is subject to birth, seeks the unborn, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. Being subject to aging, having understood the danger in what is subject to aging, he seeks the unaging ... being subject to sickness ... the unsick ... being subject to death ... the deathless ... being subject to sorrow ... the sorrowless ... being subject to defilement, having understood the danger in what is subject to defilement, he seeks the undefiled, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. Bhikkhus, this is called the noble seeking.

title: Rāhula, whatever internal earth element and whatever external earth element, that is just the earth element... whatever internal water element and whatever external water element,…
content: Rāhula, whatever internal earth element and whatever external earth element, that is just the earth element... whatever internal water element and whatever external water element, that is just the water element... whatever internal fire element and whatever external fire element, that is just the fire element... whatever internal air element and whatever external air element, that is just the air element. That should be seen with right wisdom as it really is: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' Having seen it as it really is with right wisdom, he becomes disenchanted with the air element. With wisdom, he cleanses his mind.

title: Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not have evil desires, are not overcome by evil desires, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.
content: Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not have evil desires, are not overcome by evil desires, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.

title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a genuine person is one who, even when not asked, speaks words not praising himself; what to say when asked! If asked and…
content: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a genuine person is one who, even when not asked, speaks words not praising himself; what to say when asked! If asked and required to answer, without hesitation or reluctance, he speaks words not praising himself fully and completely. This person, bhikkhus, should be understood as a genuine person. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a genuine person is one who, even when asked, does not speak words of praise for himself; what to say when not asked! If asked and required to answer, hesitantly and reluctantly, he speaks words of praise for himself, not fully, not completely. This person, bhikkhus, should be understood as a genuine person.

title: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as purified with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would…
content: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as purified with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would be reborn in heaven accordingly.' Why is that? Because his mind is purified. It is because of a purified mind, bhikkhus, that some beings here, after death, with the breakup of the body, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.
